articles.title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd break their silence on relationship in new UConn documentary
articles.summary: Dallas Wings stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are publicly discussing their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates in a new UConn women’s basketball documentary set to be released on Apple TV.
articles.body:
Dallas Wings stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are publicly discussing their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates in a new UConn women’s basketball documentary set to be released on Apple TV.

The two have always chosen to keep their relationship private, not because they wanted to hide it, but because they did not want it to define their professional careers or influence the decisions they make in the WNBA.

This small glimpse has caught fans by surprise, as many had already accepted that the pair would continue keeping their relationship out of the spotlight.

Now, however, the moment has given fans hope that they could learn a little more about the relationship between the two WNBA stars.

Fudd and Bueckers have also asked reporters to respect their privacy regarding their relationship throughout Fudd’s rookie WNBA season.

articles.title: 'Not gonna dim my light': Fever's Sophie Cunningham doubles down on trans athlete stance
articles.standfirst: Cunningham’s latest comments show the controversy surrounding her isn’t going away anytime soon
articles.summary: Cunningham’s latest comments show the controversy surrounding her isn’t going away anytime soon
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has made it clear once again that she won’t back away from her controversial views on transgender athletes, despite previously suggesting she wanted to move beyond the debate and concentrate on basketball.

Cunningham told USA Today that she doesn’t believe players or fans should be censored at WNBA games for expressing their opinions. She specifically pointed to supporters wearing “trans kids belong” shirts, arguing that the messages weren’t violent or threatening.

“None of these shirts are violent or mean,” said Cunningham . “They express [a] belief. We may not agree, and that's fine.

“I think everybody should get to wear what they want, and I think the league is making a mistake by attempting to censor anybody.”

She also challenged league leadership to take a stronger approach to the ongoing controversy, suggesting that major decisions could ultimately rest with NBA commissioner Adam Silver.

The dispute dates back to a July ESPN interview in which Cunningham rejected the “MAGA Barbie” label and explained her concerns about transgender women competing in women’s sports. She said she wanted to protect young girls in locker rooms and athletic competition from having to face what she called “biological men.”

Her comments quickly became one of the WNBA’s biggest off-court talking points, prompting criticism from players, coaches and fans while also attracting vocal support from people who share her position.

Cunningham refuses to dim her light

The controversy has also followed Cunningham into arenas. She was booed by sections of the crowd during recent Fever road games, while supporters and opponents have staged demonstrations outside venues.

Fans have brought transgender pride flags and signs supporting trans athletes, while others have displayed messages backing Cunningham .

Cunningham , however, has repeatedly insisted that the attention hasn’t changed her approach. Earlier this month, she said she wanted to get back to basketball after describing the surrounding debate as a distraction.

She previously addressed rallies organized in support of her, saying she hadn’t been involved in arranging them and viewed the demonstrations as an example of people exercising their freedom of speech.

She also argued that the WNBA had an opportunity to demonstrate its commitment to diversity and inclusion by allowing different viewpoints to be expressed.

Cunningham’s message has remained consistent, as she’s stated she intends to play basketball while also standing behind her personal beliefs.

“I’m here to play basketball, but I’m also here to be me,” Cunningham said earlier this month. She added that she wasn’t going to hide or “dim my light” simply because some people disagreed with her.

That position has made Cunningham a polarizing figure, but she doesn’t appear interested in retreating from the spotlight. As criticism and support continue to surround her, the Fever guard is standing firmly behind her views while attempting to keep her attention on the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark gets star treatment in Canada as young fan surprises her before Toronto debut
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark has become accustomed to drawing enormous crowds throughout her WNBA career, but even the Indiana Fever superstar was surprised by the reception she received before her first professional game in Canada.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has become accustomed to drawing enormous crowds throughout her WNBA career, but even the Indiana Fever superstar was surprised by the reception she received before her first professional game in Canada.

Clark’s arrival was one of the most anticipated moments of Toronto’s inaugural season. The Fever star was welcomed with plenty of excitement, but one young fan in particular stole the spotlight.

Before the game, a little girl presented Clark with a bouquet of flowers that was almost bigger than she was.

The young fan was visibly thrilled to meet the superstar after Clark signed her jersey and posed for photos with her, creating a memorable moment ahead of Clark’s first WNBA game in Canada.

articles.title: Enes Kanter encourages NBA players to enter the 2027 WNBA draft to secure better salaries
articles.standfirst: The former NBA center says the massive pay gap could motivate more players to test the league's eligibility rules
articles.summary: The former NBA center says the massive pay gap could motivate more players to test the league's eligibility rules
articles.body:
Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is escalating his challenge to the WNBA by claiming that more male basketball players could declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft if the league doesn't clarify its eligibility rules.

In a video posted Tuesday, Kanter said he'd spoken with eight players who were considering joining his campaign.

According to the former Boston Celtics player, the group includes two former NBA players, three G League players and three European players. None of those players has been publicly identified or independently confirmed Kanter's claim.

Kanter's argument centers heavily on the financial difference between the two leagues.

“Hear me out, the NBA G League pays players $45,000 a year, while the WNBA’s top players earn $1.4 million. Those ‘men’ could earn an extra $1,355,000 a year by just identifying as women. Rules are rules,” said Kanter .

The WNBA's new collective bargaining agreement has dramatically increased compensation. The league says its 2026 maximum salary is $1.4 million, while the average salary is projected to exceed $583,000. The agreement also runs through 2032 and introduces substantial salary growth across the league.

Kanter's campaign puts pressure on WNBA

Kanter first announced his intention to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft earlier this month, arguing that the league's collective bargaining agreement doesn't specifically define biological sex or gender identity beyond stating that women are eligible. Former NBA player Royce White subsequently made a similar declaration.

The controversy gained momentum after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham publicly discussed transgender participation in women's sports. Her comments triggered a wider debate among players, supporters and critics.

The WNBA has since pushed back against the campaign. Its anti-hate task force said there are currently no immediate eligibility issues involving transgender athletes and condemned what it described as “bad-faith” attempts to demean or marginalize others.

The league also said discussions about the subject would continue with the players' association.

Kanter's latest comments appear designed to increase pressure on the league by suggesting that his challenge could become larger than a two-player protest. His claim that eight additional players are considering the move, however, remains unverified, and he hasn't named the individuals involved.

The former NBA big man has also framed the dispute as more than a question of eligibility. By highlighting the enormous difference between G League and WNBA compensation, he's attempting to present the proposed declarations as a financial opportunity as well as a political statement.

Whether any other players ultimately follow Kanter and White remains uncertain. The WNBA could also revise or clarify its eligibility standards before the 2027 draft, potentially changing the circumstances surrounding the campaign.

Kanter's recruiting pitch has added another layer to an already contentious debate. What began with questions surrounding transgender participation in women's basketball has expanded into a broader confrontation over league rules and how those policies should be interpreted.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd break their silence on relationship in new UConn documentary
articles.standfirst: A new glimpse has fans wondering how much more the documentary will reveal
articles.summary: A new glimpse has fans wondering how much more the documentary will reveal
articles.body:
At the start of the season, Paige Bueckers made it clear that Azzi Fudd’s arrival in Dallas had nothing to do with her. Fudd’s selection by the Dallas Wings was the result of her own work and everything she accomplished during her time with the UConn Huskies. Being the first pick in the WNBA Draft was not about their relationship , but about what Fudd had earned and what Dallas saw in her as a player.

For that same reason, the two players made it clear that their relationship would remain private and away from the media . They asked reporters to leave their relationship out of their coverage and focus entirely on basketball.

A trailer gave fans a glimpse they were not expecting

UConn fans are getting a new behind-the-scenes look at Geno Auriemma and his program through Apple TV’s new documentary series, T he Dynasty: UConn Huskies . The three-part series shows how Auriemma turned UConn into the most successful program in college basketball .

The trailer also includes Bueckers and Fudd publicly discussing their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates. While some of what they shared had already been assumed by fans, seeing the two address their relationship in the documentary was enough to get fans excited about what else could be revealed .

Fans may finally get a closer look at the story

The small glimpse caught fans by surprise , especially after many had accepted that Bueckers and Fudd would continue keeping their relationship out of the spotlight . Now, the moment has given them hope that they could learn a little more about the relationship between the two WNBA stars.

Fudd and Bueckers have continued to ask reporters for privacy about their relationship during Fudd’s rookie WNBA season, keeping the focus on their careers while they adjust to being teammates with the Dallas Wings.

articles.title: WNBA fans blast Caitlin Clark's anthem posture while labeling Sophie Cunningham a 'true patriot'
articles.standfirst: Fans rally behind Sophie Cunningham while turning their criticism toward Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Fans rally behind Sophie Cunningham while turning their criticism toward Caitlin Clark
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has found herself at the center of another heated WNBA debate after footage from the national anthem prompted criticism from fans on social media.

The controversy unfolded before the Indiana Fever's game against the Atlanta Dream, when video appeared to show Sophie Cunningham standing with her right hand over her heart while Clark stood behind her with both hands behind her back.

Clark was facing the American flag and standing during the anthem, but her posture quickly became a talking point online. Some fans accused the Fever superstar of showing insufficient respect, while Cunningham was praised as a “true patriot” for making the hand-over-heart gesture.

One social media user described Cunningham as the only player demonstrating patriotism and criticized the other Fever players for not following the same gesture. Others went even further, directing personal criticism at Clark and arguing that athletes should always place their hands over their hearts during the national anthem.

“ Sophie Cunningham is the only good thing about the WNBA. Will support her but done with everything else,” wrote one fan.

However, not everyone agreed with that assessment. Some fans defended Clark and her teammates, pointing out that standing respectfully and facing the flag has traditionally been considered appropriate behavior. Others argued that the hand-over-heart gesture isn't necessarily the only way to demonstrate respect.

“The hand over the heart is a newer phenomenon and can sometimes be perceived as performative. Prior to the Trump year's, standing up straight in a respectful manner with your hat off worked just fine,” wrote one fan.

Anthem controversy adds to growing attention around Fever stars

The debate comes as both Clark and Cunningham continue to attract enormous attention away from the basketball court.

Clark delivered a major performance against Atlanta, scoring 26 points as Indiana secured a dramatic 95-91 overtime victory. Her performance was another reminder that the second-year superstar remains one of the biggest attractions in women's basketball.

The attention followed Clark to Toronto, where the Fever recently made their Canadian debut against the Toronto Tempo. The visiting star received an enthusiastic reception from supporters before putting together another impressive performance.

Clark scored 24 points, handed out seven assists and grabbed three rebounds as Indiana defeated Toronto 101-95. The game was played at Scotiabank Arena after the Tempo moved the contest from Coca-Cola Coliseum to accommodate the expected demand to see Clark in person.

While Clark was warmly welcomed, Cunningham received a much different reaction from sections of the Toronto crowd. The Fever forward has become a divisive figure following comments she made about transgender participation in women's sports.

Cunningham has insisted that she doesn't hate transgender people and has said her position comes from wanting to protect opportunities for biological females in women's athletics. Her comments have nevertheless generated significant criticism and support.

That backdrop helps explain why the anthem footage generated such an intense response. Cunningham already has a highly visible group of supporters, while Clark's enormous profile means even relatively routine pregame moments can quickly become viral talking points.

Regardless of where fans stand, the incident shows once again that Fever players are being scrutinized far beyond their performances on the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark feels the love from the opposition as young fan surprises her before Toronto debut
articles.standfirst: Clark may have arrived as the opponent, but Canada made sure she felt at home
articles.summary: Clark may have arrived as the opponent, but Canada made sure she felt at home
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark was surprised by the amount of love she received from fans in Canada despite stepping onto Canadian soil as the opposition . The Indiana Fever superstar has become accustomed to drawing enormous crowds throughout her WNBA career, but her first professional game in Canada gave her a different kind of welcome.

Clark’s arrival was one of the most anticipated moments of Toronto’s inaugural season. The Tempo joined the WNBA in 2026 as the league’s first Canadian franchise, giving local fans their first chance to watch Clark play a professional game on home soil.

A young fan made sure Clark’s Canadian debut came with a special memory

Before the game against the Toronto Tempo, a little girl handed Clark a bouquet of flowers that looked almost bigger than she was . The gesture quickly went viral, as the young fan got the chance to meet the superstar after Clark signed her jersey and posed for photos with her.

Whether Clark is a fan favorite or not, moments like this show what the WNBA can represent beyond teams and colors . The league is also about inspiring young girls who want to follow the same path as the players they watch on the court.

For Clark, basketball was once again proof that the game can bring people together

Clark was especially appreciative of the reception the Fever received in Canada . It was her first time visiting the country, and she left with a strong impression of the experience . She was happy to take in the culture and explore the city while seeing the excitement surrounding women’s basketball firsthand.

The Fever star thanked the fans for their support and said she had a lot of fun being in Canada . For Clark and her teammates, t he reception was a special reminder of how much the sport continues to connect people beyond the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese prove their value as their latest matchup becomes the WNBA's most-watched game of the season
articles.standfirst: The game was the most-viewed WNBA game in ESPN's network history
articles.summary: The game was the most-viewed WNBA game in ESPN's network history
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever are on a five-game winning streak and sit third in the WNBA standings , with three of their last four victories coming in dominant fashion against the Liberty , Wings , and an overtime thriller against the Dream , all teams expected to be major factors in the playoffs.

The biggest catalyst behind the Fever's soaring success is their high-octane offense, averaging 96.4 points per game , the most ever in WNBA history , led by Kelsey Mitchell ( 24.3 PPG ) and Caitlin Clark ( 22.1 PPG ), who rank second and third in points per game this season.

So far, each star has scored 20+ points in the same game 16 times this season, establishing a new WNBA single-season record for a duo .

Mitchell is currently riding a blistering streak of 20 consecutive games scoring 20+ points , while Clark, combining her scoring output with a league-leading 8.3 assists per game , is authoring the most offensively productive season the WNBA has ever witnessed.

Clark and Reese Shatter WNBA Viewership Records

The Fever don't just dominate on the hardwood; they command television screens nationwide, owning the five most-watched games of the season.

Their latest 95-91 overtime win over the Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese is now officially the most-watched WNBA game on cable in the league's 30-season history , per WNBA Communications, averaging 2.6 million viewers and peaking at 4 million .

Since Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese arrived in the league in 2024, the WNBA has experienced exponential growth in viewership.

While Clark remains the primary driving force, with the Fever starring in the most-watched broadcasts overall, the highest-rated regular-season games consistently feature matchups against Reese.

A postseason series between Clark and Reese would be the ultimate gift for basketball fans, though regardless of who Indiana faces, any Fever playoff series is guaranteed to draw record crowds because Clark's historic offensive style is unlike anything the WNBA has ever seen.
